##### `The purpose of the root damper is to smooth out any discontinuity coming from the movement component. For example when moving up a ledge / curb or falling down a small ledge, we don't want the character to 'pop' down. This effect is done in world space, unlike the pelvis offset.  Important: we don't want this damper to change the animated result when moving up a constant slope, so we only damp in the direction of the ground normal.  In order for this to work properly the correct ground normal must be fed in from the movement component.` — `EdGraphNode_Comment` (`EdGraphNode_Comment_-2684_-784_BDBDA104`)

For example when moving up a ledge / curb or falling down a small ledge, we don't want the character to 'pop' down. This effect is done in world space, unlike the pelvis offset.  Important: we don't want this damper to change the animated result when moving up a constant slope, so we only damp in the direction of the ground normal.  In order for this to work properly the correct ground normal must be fed in from the movement component.
